subject: Pharmacology
topic: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity Doxorubicin Free Radicals and Dexrazoxane
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity (Doxorubicin, Daunorubicin): Mechanism of antineoplastic action: Intercalates between DNA base pairs, inhibits Topoisomerase II-alpha, and generates free radicals. Mechanism of CARDIOTOXICITY: 1. Doxorubicin chelates intracellular iron, forming an iron-doxorubicin complex that catalytically generates HYDROGEN PEROXIDE AND HYDROXYL FREE RADICALS (Fenton reaction). 2. Cardiac myocytes express high levels of TOPOISOMERASE II-BETA. Doxorubicin targets Topo II-beta in non-dividing myocytes, inducing double-strand DNA breaks and mitochondrial biogenesis failure. 3. Cardiac tissue has very low endogenous CATALASE and superoxide dismutase levels, leaving myocytes defenseless against lipid peroxidation. Clinical presentation: DOSE-DEPENDENT DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY with biventricular heart failure. Biopsy: Myofibrillar loss, cytoplasmic vacuolization, and myocyte necrosis. PREVENTION: 1. Lifetime cumulative dose limit (< 450-550 mg/m2). 2. DEXRAZOXANE: An iron-chelating agent (and Topo II-beta catalytic inhibitor) administered to prevent anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity.
necessaryInference: Synthesize that doxorubicin causes dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy via iron-mediated hydroxyl radical generation and Topoisomerase II-beta cleavage, which is prevented by the iron chelator dexrazoxane.
strongestDistractor: Non-dose-dependent, fully reversible myocardial stunning mediated by HER2/neu receptor tyrosine kinase blockade
distractorExclusion: Non-dose-dependent, reversible cardiac dysfunction via HER2 blockade describes Trastuzumab; Doxorubicin causes dose-dependent, irreversible myocyte necrosis and dilated cardiomyopathy prevented by dexrazoxane.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Bleomycin Pulmonary Toxicity Iron-Dependent DNA Cleavage and Hydrolase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Bleomycin: Glycopeptide antitumor antibiotic used in testicular cancer and Hodgkin lymphoma (ABVD regimen). CELL CYCLE SPECIFIC: Arrests cells in the G2 PHASE. Mechanism: Binds DNA and coordinates ferrous iron (Fe2+), reacting with oxygen to generate FREE RADICALS that produce single- and double-strand DNA breaks. TOXICITY: PULMONARY FIBROSIS (subacute dry cough, exertional dyspnea, bilateral bibasilar crackles, restrictive pattern on PFTs with decreased DLCO). Dermatological toxicity (skin hyperpigmentation, flagellate erythema, hyperkeratosis). MINIMAL MYELOSUPPRESSION (spares bone marrow!). WHY PULMONARY AND CUTANEOUS TOXICITY? Bleomycin is normally inactivated in host tissues by the enzyme BLEOMYCIN HYDROLASE (an aminopeptidase). TISSUES THAT LACK OR HAVE VERY LOW LEVELS OF BLEOMYCIN HYDROLASE ARE THE LUNG AND SKIN! Therefore, unmetabolized drug accumulates in the lung and skin, producing massive oxidative injury, alveolar epithelial necrosis, and progressive pulmonary interstitial fibrosis.
necessaryInference: Synthesize that bleomycin arrests cells in the G2 phase via iron-dependent DNA strand cleavage, and selectively causes pulmonary fibrosis because lung tissue lacks the inactivating enzyme bleomycin hydrolase.
strongestDistractor: Bleomycin accumulates in lung tissue due to selective overexpression of human organic cation transporter 2
distractorExclusion: Bleomycin lung toxicity is not driven by uptake transporters, but by the innate absence/deficiency of the inactivating enzyme bleomycin hydrolase in pulmonary and cutaneous tissues.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: 5-Fluorouracil vs Methotrexate Leucovorin Biochemical Modulation
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) and Methotrexate mechanisms, and CONTRAST THE OPPOSITE ROLES OF LEUCOVORIN (Folinic Acid): 1. 5-FLUOROURACIL (5-FU): Pyrimidine analog converted intracellularly to 5-FdUMP. 5-FdUMP acts as a "suicide inhibitor" of THYMIDYLATE SYNTHASE, forming a stable covalent ternary complex with 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate (CH2-THF). This blocks conversion of dUMP to dTMP, depleting thymidine required for DNA replication (S-phase arrest). ROLE OF LEUCOVORIN WITH 5-FU: Leucovorin is administered to ENHANCE / POTENTIATE 5-FU TOXICITY AND EFFICACY! Leucovorin provides an excess pool of CH2-THF, which stabilizes the ternary inhibitory complex on thymidylate synthase, INCREASING 5-FU INHIBITION. 2. METHOTREXATE (MTX): Directly inhibits DIHYDROFOLATE REDUCTASE (DHFR), depleting tetrahydrofolate (THF). ROLE OF LEUCOVORIN WITH MTX: Leucovorin is administered as "LEUCOVORIN RESCUE" to BYPASS DHFR and RESCUE HEALTHY BONE MARROW AND GI MUCOSA from fatal toxicity.
necessaryInference: Contrast the biochemical modulation of leucovorin: it acts as a rescue agent bypassing DHFR in methotrexate therapy, whereas in 5-FU therapy it acts as a potentiator by stabilizing the covalent ternary inhibitory complex on thymidylate synthase.
strongestDistractor: Leucovorin directly accelerates the catabolic clearance of 5-fluorouracil by upregulating dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase
distractorExclusion: DPD breaks down 5-FU; leucovorin does not alter DPD, but rather provides excess folate cofactor (methylene-THF) to lock thymidylate synthase in an inactive ternary complex.

references.label: Longley DB, Harkin DP, Johnston PG. 5-fluorouracil: mechanisms of action and clinical strategies. Nat Rev Cancer. 2003;3(5):330-338. PMID: 12724731.

subject: Genetics
topic: DNA Repair Nucleotide Excision Repair in Xeroderma Pigmentosum
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate DNA Repair Pathways: 1. NUCLEOTIDE EXCISION REPAIR (NER): Repairs BULKY, HELIX-DISTORTING DNA LESIONS, most classically UV-INDUCED CYCLOBUTANE PYRIMIDINE DIMERS (thymine-thymine dimers) and 6-4 photoproducts. Mechanism: Occurs in G1 phase. Steps: (a) Recognition of distorted DNA helix by XP complex. (b) SPECIFIC ENDONUCLEASES (e.g., XPA through XPG) make cuts on both the 5- and 3-sides of the lesion, excising an oligonucleotide fragment of 24-32 nucleotides containing the damaged dimer. (c) DNA Polymerase delta/epsilon fills the single-stranded gap. (d) DNA Ligase seals the nick. DISEASE: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM (autosomal recessive). Severe photosensitivity, extreme freckling/poikiloderma, and > 1,000-fold increased risk of early cutaneous malignancies (melanoma, squamous cell, basal cell carcinoma) by age 8. 2. Contrast with: BASE EXCISION REPAIR (BER): Repairs single non-bulky base damage (deamination, alkylation, oxidation) via DNA Glycosylase -> AP Endonuclease -> Lyase/Polymerase -> Ligase. (Mnemonic: "GEL PLease"). 3. MISMATCH REPAIR (MMR): Post-replication repair of mismatched bases in S phase; defective in Lynch syndrome.
necessaryInference: Identify that Xeroderma Pigmentosum is caused by autosomal recessive defects in nucleotide excision repair endonucleases that normally excise UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
strongestDistractor: Defective base excision repair due to an inherited deficiency of 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase
distractorExclusion: Base excision repair removes single oxidized/deaminated bases via glycosylases; bulky UV-induced pyrimidine dimers are repaired by nucleotide excision repair endonucleases.

references.label: Marteijn JA, Lans H, Vermeulen W, Hoeijmakers JH. Understanding nucleotide excision repair and its roles in cancer and ageing. Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol. 2014;15(7):465-481. PMID: 24954209.

subject: Genetics
topic: DNA Repair Base Excision Repair Mechanism Glycosylase to Ligase Steps
shortestValidSolution: Master the sequential steps of BASE EXCISION REPAIR (BER): Used to repair single, non-bulky damaged bases (spontaneous DEAMINATION OF CYTOSINE TO URACIL, adenine to hypoxanthine, oxidation of guanine to 8-oxoguanine, or alkylation). Occurs throughout the cell cycle. SEQUENCE OF ENZYMES (Mnemonic: "GEL PLease"): 1. GLYCOSYLASE (e.g., Uracil-DNA Glycosylase): Recognizes and hydrolyzes the N-glycosidic bond linking the abnormal base to the deoxyribose-phosphate backbone, leaving an empty APURINIC/APYRIMIDINIC (AP) SITE. 2. AP ENDONUCLEASE: Cleaves the phosphodiester backbone at the 5-end of the AP site. 3. AP LYASE / DEOXYRIBOPHOSPHODIESTERASE: Cleaves the 3-end or removes the remaining sugar-phosphate residue. 4. DNA POLYMERASE (beta or beta/delta): Inserts the correct nucleotide (cytosine) complementary to the intact template strand. 5. DNA LIGASE: Seals the final phosphodiester nick.
necessaryInference: Trace the base excision repair pathway for cytosine deamination: Uracil-DNA glycosylase removes the abnormal base creating an AP site, AP endonuclease cleaves the 5-backbone, lyase/polymerase removes sugar and inserts correct nucleotide, and ligase seals the nick.
strongestDistractor: Nucleotide excision repair endonucleases excising an intact 24-nucleotide oligomer containing the abnormal base
distractorExclusion: Dual endonuclease excision of an intact oligomer is the mechanism of nucleotide excision repair (for bulky dimers); single base deamination is repaired base-by-base via base excision repair starting with a DNA glycosylase.

references.label: Krokan HE, Bjoras M. Base excision repair. Cold Spring Harb Perspect Biol. 2013;5(4):a012583. PMID: 23545420.

subject: Genetics
topic: DNA Repair Mismatch Repair in Lynch Syndrome Microsatellite Instability
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Lynch Syndrome (Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer, HNPCC) genetics: Autosomal dominant with high penetrance. Pathophysiology: Germline mutation in MISMATCH REPAIR (MMR) GENES: 1. MSH2 (mutS homolog 2, ~50%). 2. MLH1 (mutL homolog 1, ~40%). 3. MSH6. 4. PMS2. Function of MMR system: Functions during S PHASE (post-replication). Scans newly synthesized daughter DNA strands for base-base mismatches (e.g., G-T or A-C) and insertion/deletion loops caused by DNA POLYMERASE SLIPPAGE across repetitive nucleotide sequences. MSH2/MSH6 binds mismatch; MLH1/PMS2 coordinates endonuclease excision of daughter strand, followed by polymerase and ligase resynthesis. Loss of MMR causes MICROSATELLITE INSTABILITY (MSI-H): expansion and contraction of repetitive mono- and dinucleotide tandem repeats (microsatellites) throughout genome. Tumors: Proximal / right-sided colon cancer (ascending colon, cecum; non-polyposis, exophytic, mucinous, abundant tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes), and EXTRACOLONIC MALIGNANCIES: ENDOMETRIAL CANCER (most common extracolonic cancer in women!), ovarian, gastric, small bowel, and transitional cell urothelial cancers.
necessaryInference: Identify that Lynch syndrome is caused by germline mutations in DNA mismatch repair genes (MSH2, MLH1) that normally correct replication slippage errors in S phase, resulting in microsatellite instability and right-sided colon and endometrial cancers.
strongestDistractor: Germline mutations in the APC tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 5q causing accelerated adenoma formation
distractorExclusion: APC mutations cause Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) with thousands of polyps; Lynch syndrome is caused by mismatch repair mutations (MSH2/MLH1) and presents with non-polyposis right-sided cancer and endometrial cancer.

subject: Genetics
topic: Ataxia-Telangiectasia ATM Gene Defect Non-Homologous End Joining
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Ataxia-Telangiectasia (A-T): Autosomal recessive neurodegenerative and immunodeficiency syndrome. GENE MUTATION: Biallelic inactivating mutations in the ATM GENE (ataxia telangiectasia mutated) on chromosome 11q22. FUNCTION OF ATM: A serine/threonine protein kinase that acts as the "CHIEF SENSOR" OF DOUBLE-STRAND DNA BREAKS (induced by ionizing radiation or free radicals). When double-strand breaks occur, ATM phosphorylates p53, BRCA1, and Chk2, arresting cell cycle in G1/S or G2/M and recruiting the NON-HOMOLOGOUS END JOINING (NHEJ) and homologous recombination repair machinery. Loss of ATM leads to inability to repair double-strand DNA breaks, extreme hypersensitivity to IONIZING RADIATION (X-rays, CT scans), and genomic instability. CLINICAL TRIAD: 1. PROGRESSIVE CEREBELLAR ATAXIA (starts at age 1-2 when walking; severe atrophy of cerebellar Purkinje and granule cells). 2. OCULOCUTANEOUS TELANGIECTASIAS (spider-like capillary dilated vessels on sclerae and ears/nose appearing around age 4-6). 3. SEVERE IMMUNODEFICIENCY: Defective V(D)J recombination (which requires NHEJ!) causes dysgammaglobulinemia (LOW/ABSENT IgA, IgE, and IgG2) -> recurrent sinopulmonary bacterial infections. Markedly ELEVATED SERUM ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN (AFP) after age 8 months. High risk of lymphoid malignancies (leukemia, lymphoma).

subject: Pathology
topic: Cell Cycle Checkpoints Cyclin D-CDK4/6 Phosphorylation of Retinoblastoma
shortestValidSolution: Master the G1-to-S Phase Checkpoint (the "Restriction Point"): The master regulator of the G1/S transition is the RETINOBLASTOMA PROTEIN (Rb). 1. QUIESCENT / G0 / EARLY G1 PHASE: Rb is HYPOPHOSPHORYLATED (active/unphosphorylated). Hypophosphorylated Rb binds tightly to the E2F TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR, preventing E2F from transactivating genes needed for DNA synthesis. 2. MITOGENIC STIMULATION / LATE G1 PHASE: Growth factors stimulate transcription of CYCLIN D. Cyclin D binds and activates CYCLIN-DEPENDENT KINASES 4 AND 6 (CDK4/6). 3. PHOSPHORYLATION OF RB: The Cyclin D-CDK4/6 complex (along with Cyclin E-CDK2) HYPERPHOSPHORYLATES RB. Hyperphosphorylation induces a conformational change that forces Rb to RELEASE FREE E2F. 4. Free E2F translocates into the nucleus and drives transcription of S-phase genes (cyclin E, DNA polymerase alpha, thymidine kinase). Cell irreversibly commits to S phase and genome replication. 5. TUMOR SUPPRESSOR INK4a (p16): p16 specifically INHIBITS CDK4 AND CDK6, preventing Rb phosphorylation and freezing cells in G1. Loss of p16 or mutation in Rb causes unchecked G1-to-S progression (melanoma, retinoblastoma, osteosarcoma). CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib) stop cancer cells here.
necessaryInference: Synthesize that progression past the G1 restriction point requires Cyclin D-CDK4/6 complexes to hyperphosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein, triggering the release of E2F transcription factors to drive S-phase entry.
strongestDistractor: Cyclin B-CDK1 complex hyperphosphorylating lamins to induce nuclear envelope breakdown at the restriction point
distractorExclusion: Cyclin B-CDK1 mediates the G2-to-M transition (mitosis), not the G1 restriction point; G1-to-S entry is governed by Cyclin D-CDK4/6 phosphorylation of Rb to release E2F.

subject: Pathology
topic: Apoptosis Pathways Intrinsic Mitochondrial vs Extrinsic Death Receptor
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Apoptosis Pathways: 1. INTRINSIC (MITOCHONDRIAL) PATHWAY: Triggered by DNA damage (p53), cellular stress, withdrawal of growth factors, or misfolded proteins. Regulated by the BCL-2 FAMILY: Pro-apoptotic effectors: BAX and BAK (form pores in outer mitochondrial membrane). Anti-apoptotic guardians: BCL-2, BCL-xL, and MCL-1 (sequester Bax/Bak and maintain mitochondrial integrity). BH3-only sensors: Bad, Bim, Bid, Puma, Noxa. When stress occurs, Bax/Bak oligomerize, permeabilizing the outer mitochondrial membrane (MOMP). CYTOCHROME C LEAKS OUT OF MITOCHONDRIA INTO CYTOSOL. In cytosol, Cytochrome c binds APAF-1 (apoptotic protease activating factor-1) and procaspase-9 in the presence of dATP, assembling a wheel-like heptameric APOPTOSOME. Apoptosome activates INITIATOR CASPASE-9, which cleaves and activates EXECUTIONER CASPASES-3 AND -7. 2. EXTRINSIC (DEATH RECEPTOR) PATHWAY: Fas (CD95) or TNF-R1 binds FasL or TNF-alpha -> recruits FADD -> activates INITIATOR CASPASE-8 OR -10 -> activates executioner caspases. Cross-talk: Caspase-8 cleaves Bid to tBid, activating the intrinsic pathway.
necessaryInference: Trace the intrinsic apoptotic pathway: cellular stress activates Bax/Bak to release mitochondrial cytochrome c into the cytosol, where it binds Apaf-1 to assemble the apoptosome, activating initiator caspase-9.
strongestDistractor: Binding of Fas ligand to Fas (CD95) recruiting FADD to directly assemble the apoptosome complex
distractorExclusion: Fas/FADD activates initiator caspase-8 in the extrinsic pathway; the apoptosome is formed strictly in the intrinsic pathway via cytochrome c binding to cytosolic Apaf-1.

subject: Genetics
topic: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome TP53 Germline Mutations and Multi-Organ Carcinogenesis
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Li-Fraumeni Syndrome (LFS): Autosomal dominant cancer predisposition syndrome. GENETICS: Heterozygous germline loss-of-function mutation in the TP53 TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENE on chromosome 17p13. NORMAL P53 FUNCTION: "Guardian of the genome." In response to DNA damage (sensed by ATM/ATR kinases), p53 is phosphorylated and stabilized (dissociates from MDM2 ubiquitin ligase). Activated p53 tetramers transactivate two critical target genes: 1. CDKN1A (encodes p21 CIP1/WAF1): A CDK inhibitor that halts cell cycle in G1 phase by blocking Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and Cyclin E-CDK2. 2. BAX, PUMA, NOXA: Pro-apoptotic proteins that induce intrinsic apoptosis if DNA damage cannot be repaired. Loss of p53: Cells with extensive DNA damage fail to arrest in G1 and fail to undergo apoptosis, accumulating oncogenic mutations. CLINICAL SPECTRUM (Mnemonic: "SBLA" syndrome): Sarcomas (osteosarcoma, soft tissue rhabdomyosarcoma/liposarcoma), Breast cancer (early-onset, premenopausal), Leukemia/lymphoma, and Adrenocortical carcinoma (and brain tumors/gliomas).
necessaryInference: Synthesize that Li-Fraumeni syndrome is caused by germline TP53 mutations, disabling p53-dependent transcriptional activation of p21 (G1 cell cycle arrest) and Bax (apoptosis), producing sarcomas, breast cancers, and brain tumors.
strongestDistractor: Germline mutations in the RET proto-oncogene causing constitutive receptor tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation
distractorExclusion: RET mutations cause Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 (MEN2), predisposing to medullary thyroid cancer and pheochromocytoma; Li-Fraumeni is caused by TP53 mutations leading to sarcomas, breast, and adrenocortical cancers.

subject: Genetics
topic: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 vs Type 2 Menin vs RET Mechanisms
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) syndromes: 1. MEN TYPE 1 (Wermer syndrome): AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENE DEFECT. Caused by inactivating mutations in the MEN1 GENE on chromosome 11q13, which encodes MENIN (a nuclear tumor suppressor that regulates transcription and histone methylation). Triad (3 Ps): (a) PARATHYROID adenomas/hyperplasia (primary hyperparathyroidism, ~95%, hypercalcemia, kidney stones). (b) PITUITARY adenomas (prolactinoma [most common], GH-secreting). (c) PANCREATIC neuroendocrine tumors (gastrinoma / Zollinger-Ellison [most common], insulinoma). 2. MEN TYPE 2 (Sipple syndrome / 2A and 2B): AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT PROTO-ONCOGENE GAIN-OF-FUNCTION. Caused by activating mutations in the RET PROTO-ONCOGENE on chromosome 10q11, which encodes a RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF). MEN 2A: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (100%, calcitonin), Pheochromocytoma, Parathyroid hyperplasia (2 Ps). MEN 2B: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (aggressive in infancy), Pheochromocytoma, Mucosal neuromas (lips/tongue), and Marfanoid habitus (1 P).
necessaryInference: Contrast MEN1 and MEN2 genetics to deduce that MEN1 is caused by inactivating mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene (encoding menin), manifesting with parathyroid hyperplasia, pituitary adenoma, and pancreatic gastrinoma.
strongestDistractor: Germline gain-of-function missense mutations in the RET proto-oncogene encoding a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase
distractorExclusion: Activating RET mutations cause MEN2 (medullary thyroid cancer and pheochromocytoma); this patient has the 3 Ps of MEN1 (parathyroid, pituitary, pancreatic), which is caused by inactivating mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor menin.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors PD-1 and CTLA-4 Receptors Mechanism
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Immune Checkpoint Blockade mechanisms: Tumors evade CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell destruction by upregulating checkpoint ligands that induce "T-CELL EXHAUSTION." 1. PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH PROTEIN-1 (PD-1) / PD-L1 PATHWAY: PD-1 is an inhibitory receptor on activated CD8+ T cells. Tumor cells overexpress PD-L1 (and PD-L2). Binding of PD-L1 to PD-1 recruits SHP-2 phosphatase, dephosphorylating TCR signaling intermediates and shutting down T-cell cytotoxic killing. DRUGS: Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibodies (PEMBROLIZUMAB, NIVOLUMAB); Anti-PD-L1 antibodies (ATEZOLIZUMAB, DURVALUMAB). By blocking this interaction, these antibodies RESTORE THE CYTOTOXIC KILLING ACTIVITY OF EXHAUSTED T CELLS AGAINST TUMORS. 2. CTLA-4 PATHWAY: CTLA-4 is an inhibitory receptor on T cells that outcompetes CD28 for B7-1/B7-2 (CD80/CD86) on APCs, halting T-cell priming in lymph nodes. DRUG: IPILIMUMAB (anti-CTLA-4). TOXICITIES: IMMUNE-RELATED ADVERSE EVENTS (irAEs: autoimmune colitis/diarrhea, pneumonitis, hypophysitis/adrenal crisis, hepatitis, dermatitis). Treat severe irAEs with high-dose corticosteroids.
necessaryInference: Synthesize that pembrolizumab blocks the PD-1 receptor on cytotoxic T lymphocytes, preventing tumor PD-L1 inhibitory signaling and reversing T-cell exhaustion to enable immune-mediated tumor regression.
strongestDistractor: Direct competitive antagonism of the cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4) receptor in regional lymph nodes
distractorExclusion: CTLA-4 antagonism in lymph nodes during priming is the mechanism of ipilimumab; pembrolizumab specifically blocks PD-1 on peripheral exhausted T cells in the tumor microenvironment.

references.label: Pardoll DM. The blockade of immune checkpoints in cancer immunotherapy. Nat Rev Cancer. 2012;12(4):252-264. PMID: 22437870.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: PARP Inhibitors Olaparib Synthetic Lethality in BRCA1/2 Deficient Cancers
shortestValidSolution: Understand PARP Inhibitors (Olaparib, Rucaparib, Niraparib) and SYNTHETIC LETHALITY: 1. SINGLE-STRAND BREAK (SSB) REPAIR: Relies on the enzyme POLY(ADP-RIBOSE) POLYMERASE (PARP). PARP detects single-strand nicks and synthesizes poly(ADP-ribose) chains to recruit base excision repair enzymes. PARP inhibitors (olaparib) competitively block PARP catalytic activity and "trap" PARP-DNA complexes. 2. WHEN PARP IS INHIBITED: Unrepaired SSBs accumulate. When a replication fork encounters an unrepaired SSB during S phase, the replication fork collapses, CONVERTING THE SINGLE-STRAND NICK INTO A LETHAL DOUBLE-STRAND BREAK (DSB). 3. DSB REPAIR PATHWAYS: In healthy cells, double-strand breaks are repaired error-free via HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION (HR), which strictly requires functional BRCA1, BRCA2, and PALB2 proteins. 4. SYNTHETIC LETHALITY: In cancer cells harboring biallelic LOSS-OF-FUNCTION BRCA1 OR BRCA2 MUTATIONS (e.g., hereditary ovarian or breast cancer), homologous recombination is already defective. When PARP inhibitors block the alternative SSB pathway, the accumulating double-strand breaks CANNOT BE REPAIRED BY EITHER PATHWAY. The cancer cell is forced to use error-prone non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), resulting in massive catastrophic chromosomal fragmentation and apoptosis ("Synthetic Lethality": combining two non-lethal single deficiencies creates a lethal double deficiency).
necessaryInference: Deduce that olaparib inhibits PARP to block single-strand break repair, converting them into double-strand breaks that cannot be repaired in BRCA1/2-deficient cells lacking homologous recombination, resulting in synthetic lethality.
strongestDistractor: Olaparib directly restores wild-type BRCA1 enzymatic activity, accelerating homologous recombination repair in non-malignant cells
distractorExclusion: Olaparib does not restore BRCA1 function; it exploits the BRCA deficiency by blocking the alternative PARP pathway, killing the cancer cell through synthetic lethality.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors Imatinib BCR-ABL and Gastrointestinal Stromal c-Kit
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Imatinib (Gleevec): Small-molecule RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE INHIBITOR. Molecular mechanism: Binds competitively to the ATP-BINDING POCKET of the inactive kinase conformation, blocking ATP binding and preventing autophosphorylation and substrate phosphorylation. TARGET ONCOGENIC KINASES: 1. BCR-ABL FUSION TYROSINE KINASE: Generated by t(9;22)(q34;q11) PHILADELPHIA CHROMOSOME in CHRONIC MYELOID LEUKEMIA (CML). Fusion of BCR on chr 22 to ABL1 non-receptor tyrosine kinase on chr 9 creates a constitutively active kinase driving granulocyte proliferation. 2. C-KIT (CD117 / Stem Cell Factor receptor): Activating mutations in c-Kit receptor tyrosine kinase drive GASTROINTESTINAL STROMAL TUMORS (GIST, spindle/epithelioid mesenchymal tumors of stomach/small intestine expressing CD117). 3. PDGFRA (platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha): Subsets of GIST and hypereosinophilic syndrome. Adverse effects: Fluid retention / periorbital edema, rash, musculoskeletal cramps.
necessaryInference: Identify that imatinib functions by competitively occupying the ATP-binding site of the constitutively active BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase in CML and the mutant c-Kit receptor tyrosine kinase in gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
strongestDistractor: Monoclonal antibody binding to the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2
distractorExclusion: Monoclonal antibody targeting of HER2/neu describes trastuzumab; imatinib is an intracellular small-molecule kinase inhibitor binding the ATP pocket of BCR-ABL and c-Kit.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Trastuzumab Cardiotoxicity vs Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity Distinction
shortestValidSolution: Compare Chemotherapy-Induced Cardiotoxicities: 1. TYPE I CARDIOTOXICITY (ANTHRACYCLINES: Doxorubicin, Daunorubicin): DOSE-DEPENDENT, CUMULATIVE, IRREVERSIBLE. Mechanism: Iron-mediated free radical generation (hydroxyl radicals) and Topoisomerase II-beta cleavage. Histology: MYOFIBRILLAR LOSS / DROPOUT, CYTOPLASMIC VACUOLIZATION, and MYOCYTE NECROSIS. Leads to permanent dilated cardiomyopathy. 2. TYPE II CARDIOTOXICITY (TRASTUZUMAB / HERCEPTIN): NOT DOSE-DEPENDENT, NOT CUMULATIVE, LARGELY REVERSIBLE UPON DRUG DISCONTINUATION. Mechanism: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody against HER2/neu (ERBB2) receptor tyrosine kinase. In cardiomyocytes, HER2 signaling (stimulated by neuregulin-1) is essential for myocyte survival and stress responses. Trastuzumab blocks this survival pathway, causing "myocardial stunning" without cellular necrosis. Histology: COMPLETELY NORMAL ULTRASTRUCTURE, NO MYOFIBRILLAR LOSS, NO VACUOLIZATION, NO MYOCYTE DEATH. Manifests as an asymptomatic drop in LVEF that resolves with drug cessation.
necessaryInference: Contrast trastuzumab (Type II cardiotoxicity: non-dose-dependent, reversible myocyte stunning with normal ultrastructure) with doxorubicin (Type I cardiotoxicity: dose-dependent, irreversible myocyte necrosis with myofibrillar dropout).
strongestDistractor: Trastuzumab induces dose-dependent coagulative necrosis characterized by extensive myocyte myofibrillar lysis and sarcolemmal rupture
distractorExclusion: Dose-dependent myocyte necrosis and myofibrillar lysis describe doxorubicin (Type I); trastuzumab causes Type II cardiotoxicity, which is non-dose-dependent, reversible, and lacks myocyte necrosis.

references.label: Slamon DJ, Leyland-Jones B, Shak S, et al. Use of chemotherapy plus a monoclonal antibody against HER2 for metastatic breast cancer that overexpresses HER2. N Engl J Med. 2001;344(11):783-792. PMID: 11248153.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Vinca Alkaloids vs Taxanes Microtubule Dynamics and Neurotoxicity
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Microtubule Antineoplastic Agents (both act in M PHASE of cell cycle): 1. VINCA ALKALOIDS (Vincristine, Vinblastine): Bind to beta-tubulin and INHIBIT MICROTUBULE POLYMERIZATION. They prevent tubulin dimers from assembling into microtubules, dissolving the mitotic spindle. Toxicities: VINCRISTINE = NEUROTOXICITY (peripheral sensorimotor polyneuropathy, "glove-and-stocking" numbness, loss of deep tendon reflexes, paralytic ileus/constipation via autonomic axonal transport disruption). VINBLASTINE = BONE MARROW SUPPRESSION (mnemonic: "Vin-BLAST-ine BLASTS the Bone marrow; Vin-CRIST-ine is CRISP on the nerves"). 2. TAXANES (Paclitaxel, Docetaxel): Bind to beta-tubulin and HYPER-STABILIZE MICROTUBULES, PREVENTING DEPOLYMERIZATION. Mitotic spindles cannot disassemble, freezing the cell in anaphase. Toxicities: Myelosuppression, neuropathy, hypersensitivity reactions (premedicate with dexamethasone/diphenhydramine).
necessaryInference: Contrast the molecular actions on microtubules: vincristine inhibits polymerization of tubulin dimers (causing peripheral neuropathy via impaired axonal transport), whereas paclitaxel hyperstabilizes microtubules to prevent depolymerization.
strongestDistractor: Paclitaxel binds beta-tubulin to prevent dimer polymerization, while vincristine prevents microtubule disassembly
distractorExclusion: This reverses their mechanisms: vincristine PREVENTS polymerization; paclitaxel PREVENTS depolymerization (hyper-stabilizes microtubules).

references.label: Jordan MA, Wilson L. Microtubules as a target for anticancer drugs. Nat Rev Cancer. 2004;4(4):253-265. PMID: 15057285.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Hydroxyurea Mechanism in Sickle Cell Ribonucleotide Reductase and HbF
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Hydroxyurea mechanisms and clinical indications: 1. ENZYMATIC TARGET: Potent, reversible inhibitor of RIBONUCLEOTIDE REDUCTASE (RNR), the rate-limiting enzyme that reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs: dADP, dGDP, dCDP, dUDP). By inhibiting RNR, hydroxyurea depletes intracellular dNTP pools, halting DNA synthesis and ARRESTING CELLS IN S PHASE. Used as a cytoreductive agent in myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia). 2. MECHANISM IN SICKLE CELL DISEASE: Hydroxyurea MARKEDLY INCREASES FETAL HEMOGLOBIN (HbF / alpha2-gamma2). Mechanism: Epigenetic and transcriptional upregulation of the GAMMA-GLOBIN GENE in erythroid precursors (via nitric oxide/cGMP pathway and altered erythroid kinetics). High intracellular HbF (fetal hemoglobin) disrupts the polymerization of deoxygenated HbS (sickle hemoglobin), preventing red cell sickling, reducing vaso-occlusive pain crises, acute chest syndrome, and transfusion requirements. Dose-limiting toxicity: MYELOSUPPRESSION (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, macrocytosis / high MCV).
necessaryInference: Synthesize that hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase to deplete dNTPs (S-phase arrest) and therapeutically upregulates gamma-globin to increase fetal hemoglobin (HbF), preventing HbS polymerization in sickle cell disease.
strongestDistractor: Direct allosteric binding to deoxyhemoglobin S, stabilizing the R-state to prevent 2,3-BPG binding
distractorExclusion: Direct R-state stabilization of HbS is the mechanism of voxelotor; hydroxyurea acts by inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase and epigenetically stimulating fetal hemoglobin (HbF) production.

references.label: Ware RE. How I use hydroxyurea to treat young patients with sickle cell anemia. Blood. 2010;115(26):5300-5311. PMID: 20223921.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Cytarabine Pyrimidine Analog S-Phase Arrest and Cerebellar Toxicity
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Cytarabine (ara-C / cytosine arabinoside): Pyrimidine analog (cytidine with an arabinose sugar replacing ribose). S-PHASE SPECIFIC. Bioactivation: Phosphorylated by DEOXYCYTIDINE KINASE (dCK) into its active form, ara-CTP. Inactivation: Deaminated by cytidine deaminase (CDA) into inactive ara-U. Mechanism: Ara-CTP competitively incorporates into replicating DNA, directly INHIBITING DNA POLYMERASE (alpha and epsilon) and causing DNA chain termination. Indication: Backbone of induction therapy for ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (7+3 regimen: cytarabine 7 days + daunorubicin 3 days). Toxicities: 1. Severe pancytopenia (myelosuppression). 2. HIGH-DOSE CYTARABINE CEREBELLAR TOXICITY (dysmetria, nystagmus, intention tremor, wide-based ataxia; monitor cerebellar exams closely!). 3. Chemical conjunctivitis (prevent with prophylactic steroid eye drops).
necessaryInference: Deduce that cytarabine is bioactivated by deoxycytidine kinase into ara-CTP, which inhibits DNA polymerase during S phase to treat AML, carrying a high risk of drug-induced cerebellar toxicity.
strongestDistractor: Purine analog requiring HGPRT bioactivation that incorporates into RNA to inhibit ribosomal peptidyl transferase
distractorExclusion: Cytarabine is a pyrimidine (not purine) analog bioactivated by deoxycytidine kinase (not HGPRT) that incorporates into DNA to inhibit DNA polymerase.

references.label: Reese ND, Schiller GJ. High-Dose Cytarabine (HDAC) in the Treatment of Leukemias: a Review. Curr Hematol Malig Rep. 2013;8(2):141-148. PMID: 23512687.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Antitumor Alkylating Agents Busulfan Pulmonary Fibrosis and Marrow Ablation
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Busulfan pharmacology: Bifunctional alkylating agent (alkyl sulfonate). Mechanism: Covalently cross-links DNA at guanine bases, halting DNA replication and transcription. Clinical indication: MYELOABLATIVE CONDITIONING REGIMENS prior to allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (massively wipes out host bone marrow progenitor cells). Distinctive toxicities (Mnemonic: "BUSulfan Burns the lung, skin, and marrow"): 1. SEVERE PROLONGED BONE MARROW APLASIA (desired for transplant conditioning, but life-threatening if unrescued). 2. PULMONARY FIBROSIS ("Busulfan lung": dry cough, dyspnea, interstitial fibrosis). 3. CUTANEOUS HYPERPIGMENTATION (generalized bronze hyperpigmentation resembling Addison disease). 4. HEPATIC VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE (sinusoidal obstruction syndrome). Contrast with cyclophosphamide (hemorrhagic cystitis, minimal pulmonary fibrosis).
necessaryInference: Identify that busulfan cross-links DNA strands to achieve profound bone marrow ablation for transplant conditioning, and is uniquely associated with pulmonary fibrosis and Addisonian cutaneous hyperpigmentation.
strongestDistractor: Irreversible inhibition of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase depleting lymphocyte guanine nucleotide pools
distractorExclusion: IMPDH inhibition describes mycophenolate mofetil; busulfan is a direct alkylating agent that cross-links DNA strands and causes pulmonary fibrosis and marrow ablation.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Purine Antimetabolites 6-Mercaptopurine vs 6-Thioguanine HGPRT Activation
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate 6-Mercaptopurine (6-MP) and 6-Thioguanine (6-TG): Purine antimetabolites (thiol analogs of hypoxanthine and guanine). BIOACTIVATION: Both require HGPRT (hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase). 1. 6-MP is converted by HGPRT to thioinosine monophosphate (TIMP). TIMP INHIBITS PRPP AMIDOTRANSFERASE (the rate-limiting first committed step of de novo purine synthesis) and blocks conversion of IMP to AMP and GMP. 2. 6-TG is converted by HGPRT to 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGN), which incorporate directly into DNA and RNA, arresting transcription and replication. METABOLIC DIFFERENCE: 6-MP is inactivated by XANTHINE OXIDASE (interacts with allopurinol!). IN CONTRAST, 6-THIOGUANINE IS NOT CATABOLIZED BY XANTHINE OXIDASE; it is deaminated by guanine deaminase. Therefore, ALLOPURINOL DOES NOT INCREASE 6-THIOGUANINE LEVELS, and NO DOSE REDUCTION OF 6-TG IS NEEDED WITH ALLOPURINOL!
necessaryInference: Deduce that 6-mercaptopurine is bioactivated by HGPRT to inhibit PRPP amidotransferase, and contrast it with 6-thioguanine, which is not inactivated by xanthine oxidase and therefore does not require dose reduction with allopurinol.

distractorExclusion: 6-MP requires xanthine oxidase breakdown (and allopurinol dose reduction); 6-thioguanine is catabolized by guanine deaminase, NOT xanthine oxidase, and does not require dose reduction with allopurinol.

subject: Pathology
topic: PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry Combined Positive Score Cutoff Controversy
shortestValidSolution: UNRESOLVED CLINICAL CONTROVERSY: Comparison of PD-L1 scoring methodologies across solid tumors: Tumor Proportion Score (TPS: percentage of viable tumor cells showing partial or complete membrane staining at any intensity) versus Combined Positive Score (CPS: number of PD-L1 staining cells [tumor cells, lymphocytes, macrophages] divided by total viable tumor cells, multiplied by 100). While TPS >= 50% universally qualifies non-small cell lung cancer for single-agent pembrolizumab, the clinically decisive threshold for CPS in gastroesophageal and urothelial carcinomas (e.g., CPS >= 1 vs CPS >= 5 vs CPS >= 10) remains discordant between FDA, EMA, and NCCN guideline panels, with conflicting overall survival benefits across biomarker-stratified clinical trials. Classified as UNRESOLVED.

strongestDistractor: Absolute exclusion of PD-L1 testing in favor of universal microsatellite instability screening alone
distractorExclusion: PD-L1 testing is standard of care; the controversy centers on divergent cutoff thresholds and scoring algorithms, not abandonment of testing.

distractorExclusion: ARDS causes diffuse alveolar damage and refractory shunt (V/Q = 0); PE creates dead space (V/Q = inf) and hypoxemia via redistribution low V/Q mismatch.

subject: Physiology
topic: Hemoglobin-Oxygen Dissociation Dynamics
shortestValidSolution: Exercising muscle (high temp, high CO2, high H+, high 2,3-BPG) -> rightward shift of Hb-O2 curve -> increased P50 -> lower affinity -> enhanced O2 unloading to tissue.

strongestDistractor: Leftward shift of the dissociation curve with a decrease in P50; increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, maximizing loading of oxygen in active tissues
distractorExclusion: Leftward shifts increase O2 affinity and occur with alkalosis/hypothermia; exercise conditions (acidosis, heat, CO2) shift the curve rightward to promote unloading.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Postpartum Hemorrhage Stepwise Uterotonic Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony (boggy uterus). Oxytocin and bimanual massage are first-line. Second-line uterotonics require knowing patient contraindications: Methylergonovine is contraindicated in hypertension; Carboprost tromethamine (PGF2alpha) is contraindicated in asthma. In a patient with chronic hypertension or preeclampsia, carboprost (or misoprostol/TXA) is selected over methylergonovine.

subject: Surgery
topic: Suspected Scaphoid Fracture with Negative Initial Radiographs
shortestValidSolution: Recognize fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH) with tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Initial plain radiographs can be falsely negative in up to 15-20% of nondisplaced scaphoid fractures. Management requires thumb spica splinting and repeat radiographs in 10-14 days (or immediate MRI) to prevent nonunion and avascular necrosis.

subject: Medicine
topic: Thyroid Storm Stepwise Pharmacotherapy and Wolff-Chaikoff Effect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize thyroid storm (fever, delirium, tachycardia/afib, heart failure, jaundice). Sequence of medications: 1. Beta-blocker (propranolol); 2. Thionamide (PTU preferred over methimazole as it blocks peripheral T4->T3 conversion); 3. Potassium iodide (Lugol solution or SSKI) must be administered >=1 HOUR AFTER thionamide to prevent using the iodine as new hormone substrate (Jod-Basedow effect); 4. Glucocorticoids (hydrocortisone).
necessaryInference: Recognize thyroid storm (fever, delirium, tachycardia/afib, heart failure, jaundice). Sequence of medications: 1. Beta-blocker (propranolol); 2. Potassium iodide (Lugol solution or SSKI) must be administered >=1 HOUR AFTER thionamide to prevent using the iodine as new hormone substrate (Jod-Basedow effect); 4. strongestDistractor: Administer immediately before propylthiouracil to sensitize follicular cell iodine transporters
distractorExclusion: Administering iodine before a thionamide exacerbates thyrotoxicosis by fueling hormone synthesis, potentially inducing lethal arrhythmia or circulatory collapse.

subject: Medicine
topic: Neutropenic Fever Post-Chemotherapy Emergent Monotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize neutropenic fever: single oral temp >= 38.3 C (101 F) with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) < 500/microL. Immediate empiric monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or meropenem) within 60 minutes. Vancomycin is NOT routinely indicated upfront unless specific criteria are met (hemodynamic instability, pneumonia, catheter site infection, severe mucositis).

strongestDistractor: Combination therapy with intravenous vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ileocolic Intussusception Ultrasound Diagnosis and Air Enema Reduction
shortestValidSolution: Recognize episodic colicky abdominal pain (knees to chest), vomiting, lethargy, and currant jelly stool in a 6-24 month infant. Abdominal ultrasound is diagnostic method of choice (target / donut sign). Treatment is air or hydrostatic (contrast) enema reduction, provided there are no signs of peritonitis or bowel perforation.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma Immediate Medical Management Sequence
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute angle-closure glaucoma (unilateral severe ocular pain, headache, halos around lights, fixed mid-dilated pupil, cloudy cornea, rock-hard globe, IOP > 40-50 mm Hg). Immediate medical therapy combines topical pressure-lowering agents (timolol, apraclonidine, pilocarpine) and systemic agents (IV acetazolamide or IV mannitol). Definitive treatment is laser peripheral iridotomy.

Definitive treatment is laser peripheral iridotomy.

topic: Ectopic Pregnancy Methotrexate Candidacy versus Laparoscopy
shortestValidSolution: Evaluate methotrexate candidacy for unruptured ectopic pregnancy: Hemodynamically stable, beta-hCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, ectopic gestational sac < 3.5-4 cm, no fetal cardiac activity, patient willing to comply with follow-up, and normal hepatic/renal function. Laparoscopy is indicated if hemodynamically unstable, peritoneal signs, contraindications to methotrexate, mass > 3.5 cm, cardiac activity present, or beta-hCG > 5,000.

topic: Obstructing Urolithiasis with Urosepsis Emergent Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Recognize infected obstructed kidney (ureteral stone + fever, leukocytosis, pyuria, hydronephrosis). This is a surgical urological emergency. Immediate decompression via percutaneous nephrostomy tube or retrograde ureteral stent placement under IV broad-spectrum antibiotics. Shock-wave lithotripsy and ureteroscopy are strictly contraindicated during acute infection.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Screening and Ultrasound
shortestValidSolution: Recognize risk factors for DDH (breech presentation, female, family history) or positive Ortolani/Barlow sign. In infants < 4-6 months of age, the femoral head is predominantly cartilaginous; therefore, ultrasound of the hips is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice. Plain radiographs are only reliable after 4-6 months when the femoral head ossifies.

subject: Surgery
topic: Tension Pneumothorax Immediate Needle Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate tension pneumothorax from cardiac tamponade in trauma. Both cause hypotension and JVD. Tension pneumothorax features absent unilateral breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion, and contralateral tracheal deviation. Immediate treatment is needle decompression (2nd intercostal space midclavicular or 5th intercostal anterior axillary line) followed by tube thoracostomy, without waiting for a chest radiograph.
necessaryInference: Differentiate tension pneumothorax from cardiac tamponade in trauma. Both cause hypotension and JVD. strongestDistractor: Hold interventions until portable anteroposterior chest radiography confirms the pleural line
distractorExclusion: Tension pneumothorax is a strictly clinical diagnosis; delaying decompression to obtain radiographs frequently leads to pulseless electrical activity (PEA) arrest and death.

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Catatonia Lorazepam Challenge and Electroconvulsive Therapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize catatonia (immobility, mutism, stupor, waxy flexibility, posturing, negativism) associated with severe mood disorders or psychotic disorders. First-line diagnostic and therapeutic intervention is the intravenous lorazepam challenge test (1-2 mg IV), which provides rapid temporary relief. Definitive therapy for refractory catatonia or malignant catatonia is electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). Antipsychotics are contraindicated as they can worsen catatonia or precipitate NMS.

subject: Medicine
topic: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Diagnostic Paracentesis and Albumin
shortestValidSolution: Recognize spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (cirrhosis with ascites + fever, abdominal pain, or altered mental status). Diagnostic paracentesis shows ascitic fluid absolute neutrophil count (PMN) >= 250/microL. Immediate empiric coverage is IV third-generation cephalosporin (cefotaxime or ceftriaxone) PLUS intravenous albumin (1.5 g/kg on day 1, 1.0 g/kg on day 3) to prevent hepatorenal syndrome and reduce mortality.

subject: Medicine
topic: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Primary Prevention of Sudden Death
shortestValidSolution: Identify hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Evaluate sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk factors: prior cardiac arrest/sustained VT (secondary prevention), or major primary risk factors: family history of sudden death, unexplained syncope, massive LV hypertrophy (wall thickness >= 30 mm), LV apical aneurysm, or LVEF < 50%. Patients with high-risk features require an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD). Beta-blockers improve symptoms but do not prevent sudden death.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Pancreatitis Fluid Resuscitation and Severity Stratification
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute pancreatitis (epigastric pain radiating to back, lipase > 3x ULN). Early fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloids (Lactated Ringer's) reduces SIRS and mortality compared to normal saline. High BUN (>20 mg/dL) or rising hematocrit reflects hemoconcentration and third-spacing, predicting pancreatic necrosis. Prophylactic antibiotics are NOT indicated for non-infected necrotizing pancreatitis.

topic: Unstable Ventricular Tachycardia Synchronized Cardioversion

Immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion is required. Unsynchronized defibrillation is reserved for pulseless arrest (ventricular fibrillation or pulseless VT) or polymorphic VT (torsades).

topic: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis Diagnostic Criteria and Antibiotics
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish viral URI from acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (ABRS). Diagnostic criteria for ABRS: 1. Persistent symptoms >= 10 days without improvement; 2. Severe symptoms (fever >= 39 C and purulent nasal discharge >= 3 consecutive days); or 3. "Double sickening" (worsening after initial improvement). First-line antibiotic is oral amoxicillin-clavulanate.

topic: Preeclampsia with Severe Features Delivery Indications

Expectant management is only considered < 34 weeks in specialized centers.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Kawasaki Disease Intravenous Immunoglobulin and Coronary Aneurysms
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Kawasaki disease: fever >= 5 days plus >= 4 of 5 criteria: 1. Bilateral non-exudative conjunctivitis; 2. Mucocutaneous changes (strawberry tongue, cracked red lips); 3. Extremity changes (erythema, induration, desquamation); 4. Polymorphous rash; 5. Cervical lymphadenopathy (>1.5 cm, usually unilateral). Treatment is single high-dose IVIG (2 g/kg) plus oral aspirin within 10 days of fever onset to prevent coronary artery aneurysms.

subject: Surgery
topic: Epidural Hematoma Middle Meningeal Artery Surgical Indications
shortestValidSolution: Recognize epidural hematoma: temporal bone fracture (pterion) lacerating the middle meningeal artery, presenting with brief unconsciousness followed by a "lucid interval" and then rapid deterioration. Non-contrast CT shows hyperdense biconvex (lenticular) collection limited by suture lines. Surgical evacuation via craniotomy is indicated if volume > 30 cm3, thickness > 15 mm, midline shift > 5 mm, or GCS < 9 with pupillary anisocoria.

topic: Primary Spontaneous Pneumothorax Blebectomy and Pleurodesis

subject: Medicine
topic: Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis Probe-to-Bone and Bone Biopsy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize deep diabetic foot ulcer with positive probe-to-bone test (high positive predictive value for osteomyelitis). Plain radiographs are initial imaging (may take 2 weeks to show cortical erosion/periosteal reaction). MRI is test of choice if plain films equivocal. Bone biopsy with histological and microbiological culture is the GOLD STANDARD for identifying causative organisms and guiding targeted antibiotic therapy before initiating weeks of parenteral antibiotics.

topic: Agitation in Dementia Non-Pharmacological Management and Beers Criteria
shortestValidSolution: Recognize behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD). First-line management is always non-pharmacological (reorientation, pain control, environmental modification, toileting). Antipsychotics (atypical/typical) carry an FDA black-box warning for increased all-cause mortality (stroke, cardiovascular) in dementia and should only be used as a last resort for severe, dangerous agitation that threatens safety.

topic: Acute Limb Ischemia Six Ps and Immediate Anticoagulation
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute limb ischemia (6 P's: Pain, Pallor, Poikilothermia, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis). Sudden cardioembolic occlusion from atrial fibrillation. Immediate management is systemic intravenous heparin bolus and infusion to prevent propagation of thrombus, followed immediately by vascular surgery consultation for emergency revascularization (catheter-directed embolectomy/thrombolysis) within 4-6 hours to prevent irreversible muscle necrosis.

subject: Surgery
topic: Adnexal Torsion Laparoscopic Detorsion and Ovarian Preservation
shortestValidSolution: Recognize ovarian torsion (adnexal torsion): acute severe sudden unilateral pelvic pain, nausea/vomiting, tender adnexal mass. Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler shows enlarged ovary with heterogeneous stroma and decreased/absent venous (and arterial) flow. Gynecologic surgical emergency. Immediate diagnostic and therapeutic laparoscopy with detorsion and ovarian preservation (oophoropexy / cystectomy) is performed regardless of dusky/ischemic appearance, because ovarian tissue has remarkable recovery capacity.

subject: Medicine
topic: Carbon Monoxide Toxicity Co-Oximetry and Hyperbaric Oxygen
shortestValidSolution: Recognize carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning: headache, nausea, confusion, cherry-red skin (rare/post-mortem), normal standard pulse oximetry (cannot distinguish oxyhemoglobin from carboxyhemoglobin). Co-oximetry reveals elevated carboxyhemoglobin (HbCO > 3-5% non-smokers, >10% smokers). Immediate treatment: 100% normobaric oxygen via non-rebreather (reduces half-life from 300 to 90 min). Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) indications: loss of consciousness, carboxyhemoglobin > 25% (> 15-20% in pregnancy), severe metabolic acidosis, or ischemic ECG changes.

Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) indications: loss of consciousness, carboxyhemoglobin > 25% (> 15-20% in pregnancy), severe metabolic acidosis, or ischemic ECG changes.
strongestDistractor: Continue 100% normobaric oxygen via non-rebreather mask alone until carboxyhemoglobin is < 5%
distractorExclusion: While normobaric oxygen is the immediate initial step, pregnant patients with COHb > 15% and fetal tachycardia with loss of variability have an absolute indication for hyperbaric oxygen to prevent irreversible fetal encephalopathy.

Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) indications: loss of consciousness, carboxyhemoglobin > 25% (> 15-20% in pregnancy), severe metabolic acidosis, or ischemic ECG changes.

critique.decisiveExclusion: While normobaric oxygen is the immediate initial step, pregnant patients with COHb > 15% and fetal tachycardia with loss of variability have an absolute indication for hyperbaric oxygen to prevent irreversible fetal encephalopathy.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Laryngotracheobronchitis Severity and Nebulized Epinephrine
shortestValidSolution: Recognize croup (laryngotracheobronchitis, parainfluenza virus): barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness. Moderate-to-severe (stridor AT REST, intercostal retractions): NEBULIZED RACEMIC EPINEPHRINE plus oral/IM dexamethasone, followed by 2-4 hours observation for rebound stridor.

subject: Medicine
topic: Primary Biliary Cholangitis Ursodeoxycholic Acid Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize primary biliary cholangitis (PBC): middle-aged female, severe pruritus, fatigue, elevated alkaline phosphatase and GGT, positive antimitochondrial antibodies (AMA). First-line disease-modifying therapy is oral URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID (UDCA, 13-15 mg/kg/day). UDCA improves biochemical liver enzymes, slows histological progression of ductopenia and fibrosis, and significantly delays the need for liver transplantation.

subject: Surgery
topic: Malignant Hyperthermia Dantrolene and Trigger Discontinuation
shortestValidSolution: Recognize malignant hyperthermia: triggered by volatile inhalational anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine in patients with RYR1 mutations. Earliest sign is abrupt, unexplained rise in end-tidal CO2 (hypercarbia) refractory to hyperventilation, followed by masseter spasm/generalized rigidity, tachycardia, hyperthermia (late sign), and rhabdomyolysis. Immediate management: 1. Discontinue triggering agents; 2. Hyperventilate with 100% O2; 3. Administer IV DANTROLENE (blocks ryanodine receptor calcium release); 4. Active cooling.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Placental Abruption versus Uterine Rupture Presentation
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish placental abruption from uterine rupture in a laboring woman with a prior Cesarean scar. Placental abruption presents with painful vaginal bleeding, uterine hypertonicity/tachysystole, and dark blood. Uterine rupture presents with sudden severe abdominal pain, cessation of previously regular uterine contractions, palpable fetal parts outside the uterine contour, and loss of fetal station (fetal head recedes upward), accompanied by profound fetal bradycardia. Immediate emergent laparotomy is required.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Immune Thrombocytopenia in Children Observation versus Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize pediatric immune thrombocytopenia (ITP): previously healthy child (ages 2-5) presenting with sudden petechiae/purpura 1-3 weeks after a viral infection. Isolated profound thrombocytopenia with normal Hb and WBC. In children with cutaneous bleeding ONLY (petechiae, purpura, bruising), OBSERVATION ALONE is recommended regardless of platelet count because >70-80% achieve spontaneous complete remission within 6 months. Pharmacotherapy (IVIG or systemic corticosteroids) is reserved for active mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, GI bleeding) or life-threatening hemorrhage.

subject: Medicine
topic: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Non-Contrast Head CT and Lumbar Puncture
shortestValidSolution: Recognize subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH, ruptured saccular berry aneurysm): acute severe "thunderclap" headache peaking within seconds. Non-contrast head CT is initial test (sensitivity > 98% within 6 hours, but drops to ~85% by 24 hours). If non-contrast head CT is negative or equivocal, MANDATORY next step is LUMBAR PUNCTURE. CSF findings in SAH: elevated opening pressure, persistent RBC count across tubes 1 to 4, and XANTHOCHROMIA (yellow supernatant from hemoglobin degradation to bilirubin).
necessaryInference: Recognize subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH, ruptured saccular berry aneurysm): acute severe "thunderclap" headache peaking within seconds. Non-contrast head CT is initial test (sensitivity > 98% within 6 hours, but drops to ~85% by 24 hours). If non-contrast head CT is negative or equivocal, MANDATORY next step is LUMBAR PUNCTURE. CSF findings in SAH: elevated opening pressure, persistent RBC count across tubes 1 to 4, and XANTHOCHROMIA (yellow supernatant from hemoglobin degradation to bilirubin).
strongestDistractor: Reassure the patient that the normal CT rules out subarachnoid hemorrhage and discharge with oral sumatriptan
distractorExclusion: Discharging a patient with a thunderclap headache after a negative CT without lumbar puncture misses aneurysmal SAH in up to 5–10% of cases, leading to catastrophic recurrent aneurysm re-bleeding and death.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Septic Arthritis of the Pediatric Hip Kocher Criteria and Drainage
shortestValidSolution: Recognize septic arthritis of the pediatric hip: Kocher criteria (1. Inability to bear weight; 2. Temperature > 38.5 C; 3. ESR > 40 mm/h; 4. WBC > 12,000/microL). Emergent surgical arthrocentesis and arthrotomy/drainage is mandatory to prevent increased intracapsular pressure from causing avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

subject: Medicine
topic: Chronic Venous Insufficiency Compression Therapy and ABI
shortestValidSolution: Recognize chronic venous insufficiency (CVI): bilateral pitting edema, aching legs worse with standing and better with elevation, stasis dermatitis, brawny hyperpigmentation (hemosiderin), and ulceration over the medial malleolus. First-line conservative management: leg elevation, exercise, and graduated compression stockings (20-30 mm Hg). Crucial prerequisite: always verify adequate arterial perfusion with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI > 0.8) before applying compression to avoid ischemic necrosis.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia Pain Out of Proportion and CT Angiography
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI): severe, sudden periumbilical abdominal pain out of proportion to physical exam findings (abdomen initially soft, non-tender, non-distended). History of atrial fibrillation or recent MI. Leukocytosis and elevated lactic acidosis indicate bowel infarction. Diagnostic test of choice is CT ANGIOGRAPHY of the abdomen without oral contrast. Emergent revascularization is mandatory to prevent transmural gangrene.

topic: Erysipelas versus Cellulitis Anatomical Level and Streptococcus
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish erysipelas from cellulitis: Erysipelas involves the upper dermis and superficial cutaneous lymphatics; it presents abruptly with high fever, chills, and bright red, raised, SHARPLY DEMARCATED, indurated plaques (orange-peel appearance). The overwhelming causative organism is Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Strep). Cellulitis involves the deeper dermis and subcutaneous fat, is poorly demarcated, and has a more indolent onset.

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Bipolar I Acute Mania Mood Stabilizer and Antipsychotic Combination
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute severe mania in Bipolar I disorder (DIG FAST: Distractibility, Impulsivity/Indiscretion, Grandiosity, Flight of ideas, Activity increase, Sleep deficit, Talkativeness). For acute severe mania with agitation or psychosis, FIRST-LINE therapy is combination therapy with a mood stabilizer (lithium or valproate) PLUS an atypical antipsychotic (quetiapine, aripiprazole, olanzapine, risperidone). Monotherapy is reserved for mild mania. Antidepressants are contraindicated as they precipitate mania or rapid cycling.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome Exogenous Surfactant
shortestValidSolution: Recognize neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS): premature infant (< 32 weeks) presenting immediately after birth with grunting, tachypnea, nasal flaring, and intercostal retractions. Chest x-ray shows diffuse, bilateral reticulogranular "ground-glass" appearance with air bronchograms. Caused by surfactant deficiency (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine), leading to high alveolar surface tension, atelectasis, and V/Q mismatch. Treatment is nasal CPAP and intratracheal administration of EXOGENOUS NATURAL SURFACTANT.

distractorExclusion: While neonatal sepsis must be considered and covered, antibiotics alone do not correct mechanical alveolar collapse from surfactant deficiency; surfactant replacement is the immediate life-saving intervention.

topic: Calcium Pyrophosphate Dihydrate Pseudogout Synovial Analysis
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish CPPD (pseudogout) from gout: Pseudogout commonly affects large joints (knee in >50%, wrist, shoulder) in elderly patients, often triggered by trauma, surgery, or medical illness. Synovial fluid polarized microscopy reveals RHOMBOID-SHAPED, WEAKLY POSITIVELY BIREFRINGENT crystals (blue when parallel to the compensator axis). Plain radiographs demonstrate chondrocalcinosis (linear calcification of articular cartilage or menisci). Treatment is intra-articular corticosteroids, NSAIDs, or colchicine.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Bacterial Meningitis Dexamethasone and Antibiotic Timing
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute bacterial meningitis: fever, altered mental status, nuchal rigidity. Lumbar puncture shows high opening pressure, WBC > 1,000 (neutrophils), high protein, low glucose. Adjunctive IV DEXAMETHASONE (0.15 mg/kg) must be administered PRIOR TO OR CONCURRENTLY WITH the first dose of empiric antibiotics (vancomycin + ceftriaxone +/- ampicillin). Dexamethasone reduces subarachnoid inflammatory cascade triggered by antibiotic bacteriolysis, significantly reducing sensorineural hearing loss, neurological complications, and mortality in Streptococcus pneumoniae meningitis.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy Bile Acids and Delivery Timing
shortestValidSolution: Recognize intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP): intense pruritus on palms and soles worsening at night, in 2nd/3rd trimester, WITHOUT a primary rash. Diagnostic hallmark is elevated fasting total serum bile acids (>= 10 micromol/L). First-line medical therapy: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID (UDCA) to relieve pruritus and lower bile acids. Delivery timing: if bile acids >= 100 micromol/L, deliver at 36 0/7 weeks (high risk of sudden intrauterine fetal demise / stillbirth). If bile acids < 100 micromol/L, deliver at 36-39 weeks.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy Hemorrhagic Shock and FAST Scan
shortestValidSolution: Recognize ruptured ectopic pregnancy: reproductive-aged female presenting with acute severe unilateral lower quadrant pain, syncope/dizziness, peritonitis (rebound, guarding), and hypovolemic shock (hypotension, tachycardia). Bedside Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) reveals free intraperitoneal fluid in Morrison's pouch and the pelvis. Point-of-care urine pregnancy test is positive. This is a surgical emergency. Immediate emergent exploratory laparoscopy or laparotomy with salpingectomy without delaying for quantitative serum beta-hCG.

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Psychotic Depression Antidepressant-Antipsychotic Combination
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features (psychotic depression): severe depressed mood, psychomotor disturbance, and mood-congruent delusions (delusions of guilt, nihilism, poverty, somatic decay) or hallucinations. First-line pharmacotherapy is COMBINATION OF AN ANTIDEPRESSANT (SSRI/SNRI) PLUS AN ATYPICAL ANTIPSYCHOTIC. Antidepressant monotherapy or antipsychotic monotherapy is markedly inferior. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is first-line if severe refusal to eat/drink, severe suicidality, or catatonia.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ventricular Septal Defect Eisenmenger Syndrome Prevention
shortestValidSolution: Recognize ventricular septal defect (VSD): most common congenital heart defect. Harsh holosystolic murmur at left lower sternal border. Small muscular VSDs (loud murmur, asymptomatic) close spontaneously in >75% by age 2. Large perimembranous VSDs (soft murmur, diaphoresis during feeding, failure to thrive, hepatomegaly) cause massive left-to-right shunt. Untreated large VSDs lead to pulmonary vascular remodeling, irreversible pulmonary hypertension, shunt reversal (right-to-left), and cyanosis (Eisenmenger syndrome). Early surgical patch closure prevents Eisenmenger.

topic: Acute Diverticulitis Complicated versus Uncomplicated Management
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute colonic diverticulitis: left lower quadrant pain, fever, leukocytosis. Abdominal CT with IV contrast is test of choice. Uncomplicated diverticulitis (colonic wall thickening, pericolic fat stranding): oral antibiotics or outpatient observation. Complicated diverticulitis: Hinchey Ia (phlegmon), Ib/II (pericolic or pelvic abscess): abscesses < 3-4 cm managed with IV antibiotics alone; abscesses >= 4 cm require PERCUTANEOUS CT-GUIDED DRAINAGE. Hinchey III/IV (purulent/feculent peritonitis) requires emergent surgery (Hartmann procedure).

subject: Medicine
topic: Exertional Heat Stroke Immediate Cold Water Immersion
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish exertional heat stroke (EHS) from heat exhaustion: EHS features core body temperature > 40 C (104 F) PLUS central nervous system dysfunction (delirium, combativeness, ataxia, seizures, coma) in a person exercising in hot/humid weather. Sweating may still be present in exertional heat stroke. Immediate management: WHOLE-BODY ICE WATER IMMERSION (gold standard, cooling rate > 0.15-0.2 C/min) until core temperature reaches 38.3-38.8 C (101-102 F). Antipyretics (acetaminophen, aspirin) are strictly contraindicated because the mechanism is environmental thermoregulatory failure, not hypothalamic set-point elevation, and antipyretics worsen hepatic/renal toxicity.

distractorExclusion: Antipyretics (acetaminophen, aspirin, NSAIDs) are strictly contraindicated in heat stroke; heat stroke is caused by overwhelming environmental heat load exceeding dissipation capacity, not pyrogen-mediated elevation of the hypothalamic set-point, and antipyretics exacerbate hepatic necrosis and coagulopathy.

references.label: Lipman GS, et al. Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Heat Illness: 2019 Update. Wilderness Environ Med. 2019;30(4S):S47-S59. PMID: 31653556.

subject: Medicine
topic: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State Fluid Resuscitation and Potassium
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS): elderly type 2 diabetic, severe hyperglycemia (> 600-1,000 mg/dL), high effective serum osmolality (> 320 mOsm/kg), minimal/absent ketones, and profound dehydration (fluid deficit 8-10 liters) with altered mental status. Management sequence: 1. Aggressive isotonic IV saline (0.9% NaCl) resuscitation is the FIRST and MOST IMPORTANT step; 2. Check potassium before insulin: if potassium < 3.3 mEq/L, WITHHOLD INSULIN and replete potassium first to prevent fatal arrhythmias; if K+ 3.3-5.3, start insulin with potassium repletion.

distractorExclusion: Administering insulin before restoring potassium in a patient with serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L drives potassium into cells, precipitating fatal ventricular arrhythmias and respiratory arrest.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Phenylketonuria Screening and Dietary Phenylalanine Restriction
shortestValidSolution: Recognize classic phenylketonuria (PKU): autosomal recessive mutation in phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), preventing conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine. Manifestations: severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, seizures, hypopigmentation (fair skin/blonde hair/blue eyes due to lack of tyrosine for melanin), eczema, and a "musty" or "mousy" body odor. Newborn screening detects elevated blood phenylalanine. Management: lifelong diet strictly restricting phenylalanine and supplementing TYROSINE, initiated within the first 7-10 days of life.

strongestDistractor: Complete dietary exclusion of all dietary branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine)
distractorExclusion: Branched-chain amino acid restriction is the specific dietary therapy for maple syrup urine disease (MSUD), which presents with sweet maple-syrup urine odor and ketoacidosis, not hypopigmented PKU.

subject: Medicine
topic: Right Ventricular Myocardial Infarction Preload Optimization
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Right Ventricular Myocardial Infarction (RVMI): occurs in ~30-50% of acute INFERIOR STEMIs due to proximal Right Coronary Artery (RCA) occlusion. Classic clinical triad: 1. HYPOTENSION; 2. ELEVATED JVP with Kussmaul sign; 3. CLEAR LUNG FIELDS on auscultation. Diagnostic confirmation: RIGHT-SIDED ECG showing ST-elevation >= 1 mm in lead V4R. MANAGEMENT PRIORITY: IMMEDIATE INTRAVENOUS ISOTONIC SALINE FLUID BOLUS (0.9% NaCl) to maximize right ventricular end-diastolic volume. STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED: NITRATES, DIURETICS, AND OPIOIDS (venodilators that drop preload, precipitating fatal circulatory collapse).

distractorExclusion: Nitrates are venodilators that cause abrupt venous pooling and sharp drops in preload; in RVMI, administering nitroglycerin causes immediate profound hypotension and cardiac arrest.

subject: Surgery
topic: Aortic Dissection Stanford Type A vs Type B Management Strategy
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Stanford Type A from Type B Acute Aortic Dissection: Type A involves the ascending aorta (proximal to left subclavian artery); definitive treatment is EMERGENT OPEN SURGICAL GRAFT REPAIR due to high risk of cardiac tamponade, aortic rupture, and coronary dissection. Type B involves only the descending aorta distal to the left subclavian; initial treatment is MEDICAL MANAGEMENT with IV beta-blockers (esmolol or labetalol) targeting SBP 100-120 mm Hg and HR < 60/min.

subject: Medicine
topic: Massive Pulmonary Embolism Hemodynamic Instability Thrombolysis
shortestValidSolution: Categorize Acute Pulmonary Embolism (PE) severity: MASSIVE (High-Risk) PE is defined by acute PE accompanied by SUSTAINED HYPOTENSION (Systolic Blood Pressure < 90 mm Hg for >= 15 minutes, or requiring vasopressors). DECISIVE THERAPY: IMMEDIATE SYSTEMIC THROMBOLYSIS (intravenous Alteplase / recombinant tPA 100 mg over 2 hours) in the absence of absolute contraindications, which rapidly reduces RV afterload and restores cardiac output.

subject: Medicine
topic: Flash Pulmonary Edema Hypertensive Acute Heart Failure Management
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Hypertensive Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (Flash Pulmonary Edema): sudden massive surge in afterload and pulmonary venous transudation. Treatment: 1. INTRAVENOUS NITROGLYCERIN (sublingual followed by continuous IV infusion) to reduce preload and afterload; 2. INTRAVENOUS LOOP DIURETIC (furosemide) for acute venodilation and natriuresis; 3. Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (CPAP/BiPAP). Beta-blockers are CONTRAINDICATED during acute decompensation.

subject: Medicine
topic: Septic Shock Fluid Resuscitation and Vasopressor Selection
shortestValidSolution: Manage Septic Shock per Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines: Administer 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloids within 3 hours. If hypotension persists (MAP < 65 mm Hg) despite 30 mL/kg fluid bolus: FIRST-LINE VASOPRESSOR OF CHOICE IS NOREPINEPHRINE (potent alpha-1 with modest beta-1 support). Dopamine is avoided due to tachyarrhythmias and increased mortality.

subject: Surgery
topic: Perforated Peptic Ulcer Pneumoperitoneum Surgical Emergency
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Perforated Viscus (e.g., perforated duodenal or gastric ulcer): sudden onset of excruciating, severe generalized abdominal pain ("hit by a sledgehammer"), followed by chemical peritonitis. Physical examination shows classic acute abdomen: involuntary guarding, board-like abdominal muscular rigidity, and rebound tenderness. Upright chest radiograph confirms PNEUMOPERITONEUM: crescentic radiolucency representing FREE AIR UNDER THE DIAPHRAGM (subdiaphragmatic free air). MANAGEMENT: 1. Resuscitation (IV crystalloids, Foley catheter); 2. IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (covering enteric Gram-negatives and anaerobes); 3. Nasogastric tube decompression; 4. EMERGENT EXPLORATORY LAPAROTOMY OR LAPAROSCOPIC OMENTAL (GRAHAM) PATCH REPAIR. Do NOT order colonoscopy, upper endoscopy, or barium swallow (extravasation of barium causes fatal chemical peritonitis!).

strongestDistractor: Performance of an emergent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy to clip the bleeding ulcer base and achieve hemostasis
distractorExclusion: Upper endoscopy is strictly contraindicated in suspected or confirmed gastrointestinal perforation; insufflation of air during endoscopy massively expands pneumoperitoneum, converting it into tension pneumoperitoneum and worsening peritoneal contamination.

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia Superior Mesenteric Artery Embolism
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Acute Mesenteric Ischemia (AMI): most commonly caused by an acute EMBOLUS to the SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY (SMA, ~50% of cases), originating from cardiac source (atrial fibrillation, post-MI mural thrombus, infective endocarditis). Hallmark clinical presentation: SEVERE, EXCRUCIATING PERIUMBILICAL ABDOMINAL PAIN COMPLETELY DISPROPORTIONATE TO PHYSICAL FINDINGS (abdomen remains soft and non-tender on palpation early, before transmural infarction occurs!). Laboratory: leukocytosis, elevated serum amylase, and ELEVATED SERUM LACTATE with metabolic acidosis (indicates advanced intestinal ischemia/infarction). DIAGNOSTIC TEST OF CHOICE: CT ANGIOGRAPHY (CTA) OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS (fast, sensitive, visualizes mesenteric vascular cut-off). MANAGEMENT: Immediate IV fluids, therapeutic unfractionated heparin (prevents clot propagation), and EMERGENT SURGICAL LAPAROTOMY WITH EMBOLLECTOMY AND BOWEL RESECTION.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Pancreatitis Fluid Resuscitation and Gallstone Workup
shortestValidSolution: Manage Acute Pancreatitis per ACG guidelines: Diagnosis requires 2 of 3: 1. Epigastric pain radiating to back; 2. Lipase or amylase >= 3x upper limit of normal; 3. Characteristic imaging (CT/MRI/US). INITIAL MANAGEMENT PRIORITIES: 1. GOAL-DIRECTED INTRAVENOUS FLUID RESUSCITATION: LACTATED RINGER'S solution (200-500 mL/hr, or 20 mL/kg bolus followed by 3 mL/kg/hr) is SUPERIOR to normal saline (reduces systemic inflammation and SIRS); 2. RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND in all patients on admission to screen for gallstones/choledocholithiasis (most common cause); 3. EARLY ENTERAL NUTRITION (oral or enteral feeding as soon as ileus resolves); 4. INDICATIONS FOR ERCP: ERCP within 24 hours is indicated ONLY for acute gallstone pancreatitis with CONCURRENT ACUTE CHOLANGITIS or persistent common bile duct obstruction. Prophylactic antibiotics are NOT recommended in sterile acute pancreatitis.

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Cholangitis Reynolds Pentad Emergent Biliary Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Acute Ascending Cholangitis: infection of the obstructed biliary tree. CHARCOT TRIAD: 1. Fever/chills; 2. Jaundice; 3. Right Upper Quadrant pain (~50-70% of cases). REYNOLDS PENTAD indicates severe, life-threatening suppurative toxic cholangitis: Charcot triad PLUS: 4. HYPOTENSION (septic shock); 5. ALTERED MENTAL STATUS (confusion, lethargy). Common causes: Choledocholithiasis (common bile duct stone, most common), benign biliary stricture, or pancreatic/cholangiocarcinoma tumor. Management sequence: 1. Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation; 2. Blood cultures and immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (e.g., piperacillin-tazobactam); 3. DEFINITIVE EMERGENCY THERAPY: EMERGENT BILIARY DECOMPRESSION VIA ERCP (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with sphincterotomy, stone extraction, and stent placement) within 12 to 24 hours. Delaying decompression in Reynolds pentad carries a mortality rate approaching 100%.

subject: Surgery
topic: Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Hemodynamic Instability Management
shortestValidSolution: Manage Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA): Classic triad: 1. Severe sudden abdominal, flank, or back pain; 2. Pulsatile abdominal mass; 3. Hypotension / shock. Hemodynamic instability dictates immediate algorithm: 1. IN A HEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE PATIENT WITH A KNOWN AAA (or classic triad): IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY TRANSFER TO THE OPERATING ROOM FOR LAPAROTOMY OR ENDOVASCULAR ANEURYSM REPAIR (EVAR). DO NOT PERFORM A CT SCAN (delaying transfer to obtain a CT in an unstable patient causes fatal in-scanner cardiac arrest!); 2. In a hemodynamically unstable patient with unknown AAA: Bedside Focused Abdominal Ultrasound (FAST) in the resuscitation bay to confirm AAA, followed immediately by OR transfer; 3. Abdominal CT Angiography is reserved ONLY for HEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE patients.

subject: Medicine
topic: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Indications
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning and Hyperbaric Oxygen (HBO) indications: CO binds hemoglobin with 250x affinity of O2 (carboxyhemoglobin, COHb) and alters allosteric structure, shifting curve leftward (impairing offloading) and inhibiting mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase. Symptoms: headache, nausea, confusion, cherry-red skin, coma, myocardial ischemia. INITIAL MANAGEMENT: 100% NORMOBARIC OXYGEN via non-rebreather mask (reduces COHb half-life from 300 minutes to 90 minutes). INDICATIONS FOR IMMEDIATE HYPERBARIC OXYGEN (HBO, 2.5-3.0 atm; reduces half-life to 30 minutes, displaces CO from tissues and prevents delayed neuropsychiatric sequelae): 1. CARBOXYHEMOGLOBIN > 25% (or > 15% in PREGNANCY, because fetal hemoglobin binds CO avidly); 2. LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS, syncope, or coma; 3. SEVERE METABOLIC ACIDOSIS (pH < 7.1-7.25); 4. EVIDENCE OF END-ORGAN ISCHEMIA (myocardial ischemia/infarction, ECG changes, acute neurological deficits).

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma Immediate Medical Management Sequence
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma (AACG): ophthalmic emergency. Sudden blockage of aqueous humor outflow through the trabecular meshwork at the iridocorneal angle. Triggers: entering a dark room (pupillary dilation folds iris into angle), anticholinergics, sympathomimetics. Symptoms: sudden, severe unilateral eye pain, headache, nausea/vomiting, seeing HALOS AROUND LIGHTS. Physical exam: FIXED, MID-DILATED PUPIL, steamy hazy cornea, conjunctival ciliary injection, and a "ROCK-HARD" globe on palpation. Tonometry confirms markedly elevated INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE (IOP > 30-50 mm Hg; normal 10-21). IMMEDIATE MEDICAL THERAPY TO LOWER IOP: Combination of: 1. Topical beta-blocker (TIMOLOL); 2. Topical alpha-2 agonist (APRACLONIDINE); 3. Topical muscarinic miotic (PILOCARPINE, constricts pupil to pull iris away from angle; given once IOP < 40); 4. Systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (oral/IV ACETAZOLAMIDE) or IV MANNITOL. DEFINITIVE TREATMENT: LASER PERIPHERAL IRIDOTOMY in BOTH eyes. CONTRAINDICATION: Mydriatics (atropine, phenylephrine) are strictly prohibited!
